subject.title: Use Codex OAuth auth for ACPX isolated home

question: Should ACPX solve host Codex OAuth by copying native Codex `auth.json` into the isolated Codex home, or preserve the no-auth-copy boundary and solve the canonical issue through a different setup, doctor, or explicit-home path?
rationale: The patch crosses a credential and isolation boundary that current docs explicitly avoid, and related work shows competing shared-home and auth-materialization directions that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Repair Seeded Auth Before Merge
options.body: Require complete Codex OAuth validation, updated docs, fallback tests, and redacted live managed ACPX Codex proof before accepting the seeded-auth direction.

options.title: Use The Explicit Home Candidate
options.body: Keep this PR paused and continue the shared-Codex-home decision in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/77006 instead.

options.title: Preserve No Auth Copy
options.body: Reject auth-file copying and keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/73910 open for a setup, doctor, or upstream-supported auth bridge.

recommendation.title: Repair Seeded Auth Before Merge
recommendation.body: Require complete Codex OAuth validation, updated docs, fallback tests, and redacted live managed ACPX Codex proof before accepting the seeded-auth direction.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the best current routing candidate because recent discussion on the related explicit-home candidate reviewed the same trust-boundary decision.
